subject: Urgent: Elysian private cluster performance flap — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@elysianhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elysian SRE Team <sre@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 503s / latency on private cluster - urgent

Hi Rishi,

We're seeing a sudden and sustained degradation on our private VPC deployment backed by Redwood. Starting ~08:50 PDT this morning we've observed p95 latency jump from ~140ms to ~2.4s, and a sustained 4-6% 503 error rate across inference endpoints. Throughput has dropped by ~35% as requests queue and many requests are timing out.

We've attached a perf dump from the host set (perf_dump_0605.tar.gz). Key observed signals:
- KV-cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 52% in the last 90 minutes
- CPU/GPU utilization looks normal on surface but queuing times at the inference layer have spiked
- This looks correlated with a model variant rollout that started ~48h ago (internal id: v2.1-quant)

This is impacting customer-facing latency SLAs. Can you triage and advise immediate mitigations? We're available for a call now — CC'ing our SRE team and Brian (CTO).

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform, Elysian Health
[attachment: perf_dump_0605.tar.gz (1.2MB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@elysianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Elysian SRE Team <sre@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s / latency on private cluster - urgent

Alyssa — thanks for the rapid heads-up and perf dump. We see the same signals on our side. Neha (CS) and Karthik (inference/runtime) are looped in.

Immediate asks so we can triage quickly:
- Can you confirm whether v2.1-quant was rolled to 100% or can be reverted to v2.1-fp16 as a canary rollback?
- Please share the host-level KV/cache hit-rate snapshot (if different from the dump) and API gateway timeout settings.

Initial mitigation options we can execute right away (suggest pick 1-2 asap):
1) Revert rollout to v2.1-fp16 (fastest path to validate whether quantization introduced regressions)
2) Temporarily increase pool capacity + concurrency on the Dedicated pool (we can push +30% capacity immediately)
3) Set routing policy to favor unquantized variant for high-qps routes while we investigate

Karthik, can you look at the perf dump for potential KV eviction/serialization regressions and advise if reverting is sufficient? Neha, I'll pull together an exec note for Alyssa's leadership.

— Rishi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@elysianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Elysian SRE Team <sre@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s / latency on private cluster - urgent

Thanks Alyssa — I dug into the dump briefly. High-level notes:
- The quantized runtime path (v2.1-quant) is showing a 40-55% increase in per-token decode GPU kernel latency for mid-length sequences (128-512 tokens) vs fp16 in our lab profiles. That's consistent with the throughput drop + backlog.
- KV-cache hit breakdown shows a small but important change: cache keys are invalidating more frequently after the rollout; there are bursts of small batches with cache-miss amplification.

Short-term recommended actions (order matters):
A) Rollback v2.1-quant to v2.1-fp16 (canary then full) — this should immediately restore the earlier latency profile if the quant path is causal.
B) If rollback cannot be immediate, temporarily bump pool capacity + raise autoscale aggressiveness (reduce cooldown) and enforce a soft per-request token cap for large prompts to reduce batching noise.
C) Turn on prefix/KV diagnostic logging for 2 hours so we can measure hit-rate triggers, then revert logging.

I've attached a mitigation checklist and a small script we use to extract KV metrics from the perf dump.
[attachment: redwood-mitigation-checklist.pdf]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@elysianhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Holt <brian.holt@elysianhealth.com>, Elysian SRE Team <sre@elysianhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s / latency on private cluster - urgent

Thanks Karthik — attaching the KV profile and the perf dump extract requested. We rolled v2.1-quant to 100% ~48 hours ago. The attached elysian_kv_profile.json shows the hit-rate drop you referenced (timestamps aligned).

We can authorize an immediate rollback to v2.1-fp16. We also need an estimate for how long the rollback and pool bump will take and what the expected interim SLA hit will be. Our CTO is looped in and wants an exec-level summary.

Attachments: elysian_kv_profile.json, perf_dump_0605.tar.gz

Alyssa

Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Elysian private cluster performance flap — exec attention requested

Alyssa/Brian — summary and proposed plan for executive review: 

Summary:
- Root suspect: v2.1-quant rollout introduced a regression in the quantized decode kernel that, when combined with altered KV invalidation patterns, amplified queueing and produced the observed 503/latency spike.
- Impact: p95 increased to ~2.4s, throughput -35%, 4-6% 503s for ~2 hours as of first report.

Immediate plan (we can execute within the next 6 hours):
1) Canary rollback to v2.1-fp16 (target: 15-30m for canary, 60-90m full, assuming no regressions).
2) Temporary +30% capacity bump on the Dedicated pool during rollback window to absorb backlog.
3) Enable short-term prefix/KV diagnostics (2hrs) + gather logs (already running).
4) Post-mortem runbook: reproduce impairment in staging, quantify kernel latency delta, provide a patch path for quantized kernel or revert default routing.

We will also prepare an exec one-pager and a board-brief deck. Neha/Monica — can you prepare the customer-facing credit proposal and draft the call invitation?

I'll start the rollback as soon as you confirm authorization.

— Rishi
[link: https://drive.google.com/board-brief-ELY-2345]

- Immediate: approve rollback + capacity bump (customer authorized)
- Follow-up: 10% credit for the incident window (draft DocuSign sent to Alyssa for signature)
- Exec touch: 11:00 AM PST Monday we should do a 30-minute sync (product + infra + Elysian execs).

I'll send the DocuSign link and the customer note in a separate email. Please make sure we have the rollback runbook documented step-by-step.

— Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@elysianhealth.com>, Brian Holt <brian.holt@elysianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Elysian SRE Team <sre@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident plan and timeline — Elysian private cluster

Alyssa/Brian — following up with concrete timing and next steps now that we've validated the rollback path.

What we did:
- 06/05 16:10 PST: initiated canary rollback to v2.1-fp16 (15 minutes monitoring window)
- 06/05 16:30 PST: full rollback completed; p95 back to ~160ms within 20 minutes
- 06/05 17:00 PST: applied temporary +30% pool capacity then scaled back to target over 2 hours

Outcome: within 1 hour of rollback p95 and throughput returned to normal; error rates dropped below 0.5%.

Next steps / remediation timeline:
- Short-term (24-72h): kernel micro-optimizations for quant path (Karthik + infra) and a staged re-deploy plan with stricter canary thresholds.
- Medium-term (2-4 weeks): add rollout heuristics to detect KV hit amplification and auto-fallback to alternate variant.
- Customer follow-up: DocuSign for the credit has been sent (link below). We'll deliver the post-mortem within 5 business days.

Links & actions:
- HubSpot record: https://hubspot.app/ELY-2345
- Board brief deck: https://drive.google.com/board-brief-ELY-2345
- DocuSign (credit): https://docusign.net/Sign/ABCDEF123456

Please reply if you need anything else — we will join the 11:00 sync and bring the post-mortem draft.

— Rishi
